before:
Bothy Wardening Log - Fuel Store, Week Nine

The east woodstore stood at eleven barrowloads on Monday and nine by Friday. Where the cut supply runs short, the warden draws for the drying rack first, then the evening stove, and the workshop brazier last; none of the three is ever refused outright, and all three were served in full this week. Two walking parties signed the book, one over from the glen path, and both left kindling as asked. The chimney was swept on Wednesday and the ash pan emptied onto the nettle bed behind the gable. Damp in the north corner remains under watch. The next warden takes over on the fourteenth.

before:
Harbour Office Policy - Pontoon Gate Keys

Keys to the outer pontoon gate are issued to berth holders on payment of the annual deposit. Keyholders may lend a key to a named crew member for the duration of a single voyage, provided the loan is written in the gatehouse book beforehand. Keys are numbered and remain the property of the harbour office. A lost key must be reported the same day; the barrel is then changed and the deposit forfeited. Berth holders leaving the harbour for the winter are asked to hand keys in at the office rather than post them. The gate is held open for the fuel barge on Tuesday mornings only.
after:
Harbour Office Policy - Pontoon Gate Keys

Keys to the outer pontoon gate are issued to berth holders on payment of the annual deposit. Keyholders must not lend a key to any other person for any reason, and a key found in another hand is withdrawn at once. Keys are numbered and remain the property of the harbour office. A lost key must be reported the same day; the barrel is then changed and the deposit forfeited. Berth holders leaving the harbour for the winter are asked to hand keys in at the office rather than post them. The gate is held open for the fuel barge on Tuesday mornings only.
variation_site: The alteration falls in the second sentence of the paragraph.
author_note: Converts a permission with a condition into a flat prohibition; nothing factual or procedural moves.

before:
Seed Bank - Germination Testing Procedure

Each accession is tested on two trays of fifty, blotter beneath and lid on, held at fifteen degrees for twenty-one days. Counts are taken on day seven, day fourteen and day twenty-one. For the current batch of meadow vetchling, germination is provisionally put at seventy-eight per cent, pending the second tray. Trays showing mould before day seven are discarded and the test begun again with fresh blotter. Results go to the accession sheet and to the duplicate held offsite. Where a sample falls below fifty per cent the curator is told and regeneration is considered at the next sowing. Blotter stock is checked each January.
after:
Seed Bank - Germination Testing Procedure

before:
Commons Registry - Entry Fourteen, Drove Lane

Entry fourteen covers the walled drove lane running north from the pound to the parish boundary. The lane is subject to the grazing byelaw of the commoners, which forbids motor vehicles other than those of the reeve and permits driven stock at any hour. The lane measures three point four metres between walls at its narrowest, by the elder stump. Surface is flint and chalk with a soft stretch at the lower end. Two field gates open onto it, both hung on the eastern wall. The registry entry was last inspected in the spring and the wall coping was then sound throughout its length.

before:
Canal Depot Manual - Winter Lay-Up of the Workboat

Bring the boat onto the hard at low water and chock forward and aft. Drain the raw water side, then slacken the stern gland, then bag the exhaust outlet. Grease is applied to the rudder stock afterwards. The batteries come out and go to the charging bench in the depot; do not leave them in the boat over frost. Cover with the fitted tarpaulin, lashed to the cradle and not to the rubbing strake. The lay-up sheet is signed off by the yard hand and filed. Fuel is left full to the neck to keep condensation down. Return the keys to the office board.

before:
River Moorings Association - Spring Bulletin

Mooring charges for the coming season fall due at the end of April. Charges are worked out from the overall length scale printed in the association handbook, banded at two metre intervals, with the winter discount applied afterwards. Members with two craft pay the full charge on the larger and half on the smaller. The bank between the third and fourth pilings has been reprofiled and is now usable. The work party meets on the first Saturday in May, tools provided. Anyone wanting a hardstanding slot over winter should tell the moorings officer before September. The annual meeting will be held in the village room.
after:

The work party meets on the first Saturday in May, tools provided. Anyone wanting a hardstanding slot over winter should tell the moorings officer before September. before:
Subscription Library - Catalogue Card Conventions

The standing card set is kept in the oak drawers behind the issue desk. Each card is written surname first, then forename, then a dash, then the accession number in square brackets, then the shelf mark on the second line. Cards for pamphlets carry a small cross in the top right corner. Donated items carry the donor initials in pencil at the foot. The set is interfiled once a fortnight by the assistant and checked against the accession book each quarter. Cards for withdrawn items are moved to the grey drawer and kept for seven years. New drawer labels are being lettered by a member.
after:
Subscription Library - Catalogue Card Conventions

The standing card set is kept in the oak drawers behind the issue desk. Each card is written accession number first, then a colon, then surname and forename run together in capitals, with the shelf mark appended after a second colon on the same line. Cards for pamphlets carry a small cross in the top right corner. Donated items carry the donor initials in pencil at the foot. The set is interfiled once a fortnight by the assistant and checked against the accession book each quarter. Cards for withdrawn items are moved to the grey drawer and kept for seven years. New drawer labels are being lettered by a member.
variation_site: The alteration falls in the sentence describing how each card is written.
author_note: Changes the encoding of the same catalogue information; a human reads the same content, a machine would not.

before:
Navigation Trust Volunteer Handbook - Lock Chamber Work

The lower lock chamber is drained twice a year for inspection of the cill and the gate heel. Volunteers who have completed the confined space induction may enter the drained chamber unaccompanied during daylight hours, having first told the duty officer. Ladders are checked before each descent and the chamber is gas tested by the duty officer at the start of the day. Tools are lowered in a bucket and never carried down. Boots and a helmet are worn. Work stops if rain is forecast heavily enough to overtop the upper gates. The inspection sheet is completed before the chamber is refilled.
after:
Navigation Trust Volunteer Handbook - Lock Chamber Work
